facts_found: Profile updates including email address are handled by Rho-Bank support (e.g., the dedicated senior support team lists 'Profile updates (mailing address, phone, email) and communication preferences' among services). [doc_checking_accounts_gold_years_account_005]
Before discussing or changing account details, support verifies the customer's identity using standard authentication steps. [doc_checking_accounts_gold_years_account_005]
Customers should have ready their full name as it appears on the account and a government-issued ID nearby for verification if requested. [doc_checking_accounts_gold_years_account_005]

Rho-Bank will never ask for the customer's online or mobile banking password, and one-time passcodes should not be shared except when actively signing in or verifying a customer-initiated transaction. [doc_checking_accounts_gold_years_account_005]
Sensitive information should be sent via secure messaging within digital banking rather than regular email. [doc_checking_accounts_gold_years_account_005]

Identity verification is recorded using the log_verification tool, which has fields: name, user_id, address, email, phone_number, date_of_birth, and time_verified (time_verified must reflect the precise moment verification was completed). [doc_customer_support_special_support_codes_001]

Internal procedures for account changes consistently require verifying the customer's identity using standard verification procedures before acting. [doc_credit_cards_credit_card_account_logistics_002]

Customers can keep contact information current via their profile/notification settings; email and notification preferences are confirmed in the profile. [doc_business_checking_accounts_hunter_green_008]

facts_found: Profile updates (mailing address, phone, email) and communication preferences are handled by the dedicated senior support team, which verifies identity using standard authentication steps before discussing account details. [doc_checking_accounts_gold_years_account_005]

Customers are told to have their full name as it appears on the account and a government-issued ID nearby 'for verification if requested' — the KB does not state that presenting a government ID substitutes for the standard verification fields. [doc_checking_accounts_gold_years_account_005]

The only documented alternative verification credential is the Account Recovery Bypass Code, and its scope is limited to identity verification for Rho-Bank account recovery. [doc_customer_support_special_support_codes_001]

The Account Recovery Bypass Code must be used only for account recovery, must match exactly, must not be combined with additional personal data collection in the same verification event, and if it does not match the agent must revert to standard verification or escalate per queue policy. [doc_customer_support_special_support_codes_001]

When a bypass code is used, log_verification is populated with the code value in name, user_id, address, email, phone_number and date_of_birth, with time_verified set to the actual verification timestamp; no customer personal details are entered. [doc_customer_support_special_support_codes_001]

Human transfer reason code 'account_ownership_dispute' is explicitly for 'Ownership disputes, joint account issues, or identity verification failures requiring specialist' and is a Tier 1 (highest priority) reason for the transfer_to_human_agents tool. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_042]

Human transfer reason code 'fraud_or_security_concern' (Tier 1) covers fraud, identity theft, unauthorized transactions, or security concerns requiring specialist handling. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_042]

Escalation to the security team is required when a customer cannot verify their identity or when the agent suspects the person contacting support may not be the actual account holder (stated in the debit-card security-alert procedure). [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_039]

'Enhanced verification' (full name + date of birth + last 4 of SSN + confirmation of 2-3 recent transactions, or security questions) is documented only for debit-card stolen-card and high-risk PIN-lock scenarios, not for profile/email updates. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_037]

In-person verification with valid ID at a Rho-Bank branch is documented as the fallback for card security restrictions, not as a documented route for email profile updates. [doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_037]

Rho-Bank support will never ask for the customer's online or mobile banking password, and one-time passcodes should not be shared except when actively signing in or verifying a customer-initiated transaction — so neither a password nor an OTP to the new address is a valid verification method. [doc_checking_accounts_gold_years_account_005]

Sensitive information must be sent via secure messaging within digital banking rather than regular email; secure message and call-back are the documented contact channels for profile-update requests. [doc_checking_accounts_gold_years_account_005]

The KB contains no procedure or policy describing an alternative/secondary verification path specifically for an email profile update when the customer cannot supply two of the four standard fields (DOB, email, phone, address). [doc_customer_support_special_support_codes_001]

open_questions: No KB document defines the standard verification rule itself (e.g., that two of the four fields DOB/email/phone/address must match) or any documented exception when a customer can supply fewer than two.

No KB document states whether security questions, last-4 SSN, or government-ID review are permitted as substitutes for the standard fields on a profile/email update (they are documented only for debit-card security scenarios).
No KB document confirms whether the Account Recovery Bypass Code may ever be applied to a profile update (the document restricts it to account recovery).

Still unresolved from earlier: the dedicated step-by-step email-change procedure, the tool name/parameters used to update a customer's email address, and whether a confirmation link must be sent to the new email before the change takes effect.
No documented service level, callback verification window, or branch in-person process specifically for failed profile-update verification.
